info.description:
Management API for reverse-proxy sites across one or more NGINX hosts.

Authentication is OIDC: obtain an access token from Keycloak and send it as
a bearer token. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents; branch on the stable
`type` URI rather than on the human-readable `detail`.
info.title: Easy NGINX Admin API

get.description: Requires global ADMIN: the trail spans every domain in the estate. Narrow the time range where possible — it lets PostgreSQL skip whole monthly partitions.

get.summary: The actions that can appear in the trail, for building a filter

post.description: Available only when local authentication is enabled. Rate limited as a sensitive operation, and every rejection returns the same message whether the account is missing, disabled or the password is wrong.
post.summary: Exchange a username and password for an access token

get.description: Unauthenticated: a login screen has to render before anyone has a token. Returns only what a login page needs — never whether an account exists.
get.summary: Which authentication methods this deployment offers

get.description: Metadata only. Private key material is never returned by any endpoint.

post.description: Validates with HTTP-01 against the managed NGINX hosts. Wildcards need DNS-01 and are refused. Requires MANAGE over the namespace of every domain requested, because a certificate is authority to terminate TLS for that name.

For a key rotation or a change of key provider. Every secret records the key that wrapped it, so keep the previous key or provider configured until this reports nothing left to do — then it can be removed. Resumable: a secret that cannot be read is counted and skipped, not retried forever.
post.summary: Re-encrypt stored private keys under the current key-encryption key

post.description: The domains and dates are read from the certificate, not from the request. Uploaded certificates are never renewed automatically; the platform has no relationship with whoever issued them.

delete.description: Refused while any proxy site still references it.

post.description: Renewal normally happens on its own inside the renewal window. This forces it, and counts against the authority's rate limits like any other request.
Asks the issuing authority to revoke it where that is supported, and marks it unusable here either way. Revoked material is never deployed.

get.description: Private key material is excluded from the file list at every permission level.

get.summary: Fetch one deployment with its phase history

post.description: Queues a new deployment of the previous bundle. Rollback is never automatic: the only automatic revert is the agent restoring the previous release when a reload fails, which is a refusal to leave the host broken.
post.summary: Re-activate the configuration this deployment replaced

get.description: With siteId, only the groups that site is filed under — which is what a site's own page needs, and cannot otherwise be answered without asking every group in turn.
get.summary: List domain groups visible to you

post.description: A top-level group requires global MANAGE; a subgroup requires MANAGE on its parent.

delete.description: Refused while the group has subgroups or members, because deleting it would silently revoke every grant made over it.

put.description: The path is identity and cannot be changed: moving a group would silently change which sites every grant beneath it reaches.

get.description: Returns each site's domain, not only its id: a caller given bare ids has to resolve every one of them to show a list, and is the party least able to do that in a single query.
get.summary: List the sites in a group

delete.summary: Remove a site from a group

post.description: Requires MANAGE on both the group and the site. Requiring only the group would let someone add a site they have no rights to and inherit control of it.
post.summary: Add a site to a group

get.summary: List Keycloak groups seen in tokens

post.description: Requires global admin: a local account carries global roles, so anyone able to create one could otherwise grant themselves SUPER_ADMIN.

delete.description: Refused for the last enabled administrator.

put.summary: Update a local account's profile, roles and groups

post.description: Refused for the last enabled administrator, which would lock everyone out.

put.description: Changing your own requires the current password. An administrator resetting someone else's does not, and must not — a reset exists precisely for the case where the old password is unavailable.

post.description: Restricted to SUPER_ADMIN: registering a host decides where configuration is deployed.

put.description: The fingerprint is pinned in addition to CA verification, so replacing an agent's certificate makes the host unreachable until this is called. Swap the certificate on the host first, then call this: the window between the two is a loss of control, never of traffic — the host keeps serving throughout.
put.summary: Trust a new agent certificate for this host

get.summary: Recent configuration bundles for an instance, newest first

get.description: Filter by scope with groupId or siteId. Listing every grant requires global ADMIN.

post.description: Requires ADMIN on the target scope, and you may never grant more than you hold.

get.summary: Your effective permission on a site

post.description: Authorised exactly like creating the grant. Answers the question a wildcard pattern hides: '*.example.com' at MANAGE is one line of configuration and authority over every subdomain, including ones created later. The list is what the scope reaches today; coversFutureDomains says whether it will keep admitting new ones.
post.summary: Show what a grant would reach, without creating it

get.description: Filtering, sorting and pagination are applied in the query, never over an already-fetched page. Sort as sort=domain,asc; repeat the parameter for multiple sorts.

put.description: Send the version last read as If-Match to have concurrent edits rejected.

post.description: The copy is created disabled so a half-edited duplicate cannot take traffic.
Returns 202: the bundle is rendered from current state and applied by the dispatcher, so the response arrives before the host has been changed. Poll the deployment for the outcome.
post.summary: Deploy the NGINX instance this site belongs to

delete.summary: Remove the expiry so the site never expires

get.description: Renders without deploying, and reports which files would change on the host.
get.summary: Show the configuration this site would produce

get.description: Advisory. NGINX Open Source resolves upstream names once when the configuration loads, so a reachable upstream now may still fail later; this catches a typo or a service that is not running. The probe runs on the NGINX host, which is where the answer means something and where NGINX will connect from — the management server never dials a user-supplied address.
get.summary: Ask the host whether this site's upstreams accept a connection

get.description: A convenience index for grant authoring. Authorization never reads it: roles and group membership always come from the caller's token. Paged and searchable because this gains a row for every person who ever signs in and loses one only when the platform deletes an account it owns.
get.summary: Search users who have signed in
